lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 3: Full Cycle of a Deep Learning Project

unit.name: Deployment tradeoffs: VAD, edge/cloud cost, and frame quality
unit.description: Uses visual activity detection to show how deployment constraints create engineering choices beyond the main face-recognition model.
unit.summary: A deployed face-recognition system cannot usually stream video 24/7 to the cloud and classify every frame because the cost and latency would be too high [ts=2247s]. Visual Activity Detection is introduced as a low-cost, low-power step that decides whether an image is worth sending to the larger recognition model [ts=2319s]. The lecture compares a quick non-ML pixel-change threshold with a smaller neural network for detecting whether a human is present, arguing that the fast baseline is often a good first step because it can be implemented and tested quickly [ts=2416s]. Real deployment exposes additional discoveries, such as selecting several high-resolution, in-focus frames from a video sequence to improve recognition accuracy [ts=3036s].

key_points.text: Streaming video continuously to the cloud for every-frame recognition is often too expensive or too slow.
Visual Activity Detection is a low-cost prefilter that decides whether to invoke the more expensive face-recognition system.
A simple VAD baseline can count how many pixels changed compared with a previous frame and threshold that fraction.
A lightweight neural network can be trained to detect whether a human is present, but it requires more implementation effort than the quick baseline.
The fastest implementation can reveal real deployment failure modes such as trees, cars, cats, or blurry frames.
Selecting clear, high-resolution, in-focus frames can significantly improve downstream face-recognition quality.

kp_catalog.name: Deployment as model-serving software
kp_catalog.description: A trained model becomes a software service or local component that accepts inputs, runs inference, and returns product decisions under cost and latency constraints.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Deployment constraints motivate VAD, edge/cloud choices, and monitoring; the lecture explicitly distinguishes a trained model from a deployed product [ts=2211s] [ts=2247s].

kp_catalog.name: Visual Activity Detection prefilter
kp_catalog.description: Visual Activity Detection is a cheap prefilter that decides whether a camera frame should be processed by a more expensive face-recognition model.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The VAD prefilter is a concrete deployment example used to illustrate lifecycle tradeoffs.

kp_catalog.name: Frame-quality selection for vision systems
kp_catalog.description: In video-based recognition, selecting clear, high-resolution, in-focus frames can materially improve downstream model accuracy.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Frame-quality selection is a narrow implementation tactic within the VAD example.
